newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 20.

text.p: Japanese semiconductor makers, including NEC Corp, plan to scale down production of 16-megabit dynamic random access memory chips (DRAMs) due to a sharp decline in memory chip prices, while U.S. and South Korean chip makers, including Micron Technology Inc, plan to boost production. NEC will reduce monthly output toward the end of next year after increasing it from the present 12 million chips to 15 million next summer.
Five major warehouse operators are expected to see their pre-tax profit stay flat in the year to March 1997 due to sluggish domestic demand and slowing international trade.

Four leading ink makers are expected to see bigger pre-tax profits in the year to March 1997, helped by cost cuts and lower interest payments. Toyo Ink Manufacturing Co Ltd expects to increase pre-tax profit by 13 percent to 6.2 billion yen, while Sakata Inx Corp expects a 24 percent rise in pre-tax profit to 2.9 billion yen.

Major pump maker Torishima Pump Manufacturing Co Ltd is expected to increase its pre-tax profit by nine percent to 1.35 billion yen in the year to March 1997 due to lower interest payments and a good start in new business, while another major pump maker, DMW Corp, is likely to see a 32 percent fall in earnings to 1.13 billion yen.
